sites.rationale: GALR2 is a GPCR with no endogenous signal peptide; EC1 (residues 1–25) is the sole extracellular terminus. The published construct prepends an exogenous HA signal sequence and FLAG before residue 1 of the full-length receptor; after HA-SP cleavage the FLAG is at the extracellular N-terminus. Because no residue number is named in the clip, the position is topology-derived: the prepend junction (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M) is the only possible extracellular terminus. The tag is 26 residues from TM1, well above the 3-residue minimum. Full-length human GALR2 cloned into pcDNA3.1(+) with an exogenous N-terminal HA signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope tag (DYKDDDDK); after HA-SP cleavage the FLAG is displayed at the extracellular N-terminus of the membrane-anchored receptor. GALR2 has no endogenous signal peptide (EC1 = residues 1–25), so the only extracellular terminus is the N-terminus and the tag must prepend residue 1.

sources.claim: The human GALR1 and GALR2 were cloned into pcDNA3.1(+) vector (Thermo Fisher Scientific) with an N-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) signal sequence and a FLAG epitope tag (DYKDDDDK).

literature_notes: L2 (PMC7108740) describes chimeric GALR2/GALR3 receptors carrying HiBiT tags confirmed on the plasma membrane by Nano-Glo extracellular detection. This clip was not used to propose a site because: (1) the constructs are chimeric, not pure GALR2; (2) no residue or loop is named for the HiBiT insertion point; (3) the clip cannot be pinned to any specific junction in GALR2. The C6 cysteine in EC1 is noted but is not disrupted by a prepend tag at position 0. The large intracellular C-terminus (IC4, residues 296–387) is not a surface site and is not proposed.
